comments: Remarkably thorough ablation revealing that feature-guided prompting is not just ineffective but counterproductive; generators (Qwen, Phi, DeepSeek) over/under-comply with constraints in model-specific ways.

model_io.model: LLM-based synthetic data augmentation (Qwen2.5-7B, Phi-3.5, DeepSeek-R1) with stylistic constraints
inputs: seed real headlines (GossipCop-PolitiFact, 23,196 samples), 15 stylistic feature constraints
outputs: 5,000 synthetic fake-news headlines per generator condition

hypotheses.hypothesis: Individual stylistic constraints improve synthetic data augmentation effectiveness
hypotheses.result: Refuted; no constraint is necessary or sufficient; F1 differences <0.02 across all 15 ablations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Full stylistic guidance improves alignment with real fake-news distributions
hypotheses.result: Refuted; full prompt increased question marks 5.3× (Qwen), reduced ALL CAPS 12.5×, distorting rather than improving alignment

title: Orthogonally regulated multi-timescale reservoir and linear nonvolatile readout in a vertical transistor for dynamic machine vision
task: Implementing orthogonally regulated multi-timescale reservoir computing with nonvolatile ferroelectric readout in vertical organic FET
key_results: >90% accuracy on dynamic human-action recognition; ferroelectric readout achieves >10⁶ endurance, >3000 s retention, 0.31±0.05 asymmetry nonlinearity; on/off ratio ~10⁷
comments: Innovative monolithic integration decoupling volatile dynamics from nonvolatile storage, though edge-device power consumption and latency for real-time tasks are not quantified.

model_io.model: Fe-vOFET with Rubrene/F16CuPc heterojunction and MFMIS stack

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orthogonal decoupling of photocarrier dynamics and ferroelectric polarization enables simultaneous reservoir nonlinearity and readout linearity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dual-mode operation achieves >90% action-recognition accuracy with linear, symmetric weight updates

title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr2
task: Electrically tunable second-harmonic generation using ferroelectric NbOBr₂ integrated on silicon nitride chip
key_results: SHG conversion efficiency 158% W⁻¹, 53% electrical modulation depth, non-volatile multi-level polarization control with >10⁶ endurance
comments: Novel integration of ferroelectric switching with nonlinear optics for integrated photonics, though the thickness-dependent efficiency scaling mechanism could be better explained.

model_io.model: Fe-NbOBr₂/SiN microring resonator with Schottky interface

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ferroelectric polarization switching modulates Schottky barrier, controlling carrier injection and nonlinear response
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SHG efficiency tunable via ferroelectric control with 53% modulation depth

title: Active-flow-driven DNA remodelling generates millimetre-scale mechanical oscillations
task: Generating rhythmic mechanical oscillations through active flows in DNA-microtubule composites
key_results: Sharp non-equilibrium transition from disordered to millimetre-scale synchronized oscillatory flow tuned by DNA contour length; oscillation frequency agrees with active-gel model predictions
comments: Elegant demonstration of autonomous self-organization via mechanical feedback without chemical signalling, though the biological relevance to actual gene regulation remains to be established.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Interplay between activity, orientational order, and self-generated viscoelasticity drives oscillatory instability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; sharp transition and frequency scaling match theoretical predictions

title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
task: Engineering bound states in the continuum via quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
key_results: Friedrich–Wintgen BIC realized through coherent coupling of two Feshbach resonances using Floquet engineering; colliding atoms become transparent to one another at critical parameter point
comments: Elegant quantum-interference demonstration with non-Hermitian physics implications, though practical applications beyond fundamental physics remain unclear.

model_io.model: Ultracold ⁶Li collisions with Floquet-engineered Feshbach resonances

hypotheses.hypothesis: Destructive quantum interference between two Feshbach resonances produces a state localized within the scattering continuum
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Friedrich–Wintgen BIC observed with elastic and inelastic coupling vanishing at critical point

title: Design of an ultra low voltage VDBA using bulk driven quasi floating gate techniques for high order biosignal processing
task: Designing ultra-low-voltage VDBA for biosignal filtering using bulk-driven techniques
key_results: 0.5-V operation consuming 370 nW; fifth-order Butterworth filter achieves 73.65–557.8 Hz electronically tunable cutoff, 1.1% THD, 44 dB dynamic range
comments: Well-engineered subthreshold design validated by both simulation and discrete implementation, though the 44 dB dynamic range limits clinical-grade ECG acquisition.

outputs: filtered ECG (73.65–557.8 Hz), THD, dynamic range

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bulk-driven and BD-QFG techniques overcome threshold-voltage limitations in subthreshold operation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; robust performance in Monte Carlo and PVT analyses

title: High-accuracy graphene quantum Hall array resistance standards based on wye-delta transformation
task: High-accuracy graphene quantum Hall resistance standards using wye-delta transformation with minimal hall bars
key_results: Quantization to 80 nΩ/Ω at 1–100 MΩ range; LHe-free operation achievable at 1.6 K with accuracy of few parts in 10⁸
comments: Significant progress toward portable quantum resistance standards, though the 5–6 T field requirement remains impractical compared to 14+ T traditional systems.

model_io.model: Graphene Y-Δ Hall-bar array (28 bars per device)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Y-Δ transformation reduces hall-bar count while maintaining quantization accuracy through triple-connection topology
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 28-bar device achieves 80 nΩ/Ω accuracy without cryogenic current comparator

title: Examining cyclic modulation of hormones, immune cells and microbiota profiles during the menstrual cycle in Macaca mulatta
task: Characterizing hormonal, immune, and microbial dynamics across menstrual cycles in females
key_results: Estradiol peaked at ovulation and progesterone during luteal phase with high consistency; cervicovaginal leukocytes positively associated with estradiol elevation; vaginal microbiota composition and diversity remained stable across cycles with interindividual variability dominating over hormonal effects
comments: While the study provides valuable longitudinal data on female physiology, the small sample size (n=6) and focus on a single primate species may limit generalizability; the finding that menstrual cycling introduces minimal variability is important for improving female representation in preclinical research but requires validation in other animal models and humans.

model_io.model: Menstrual cycle tracking in rhesus macaques
inputs: systemic hormone levels (estradiol, progesterone, testosterone, cortisol)
peripheral immune cell populations (CD45+, CD4+, CD8+, CD56+, CD123+)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Menstrual cycle hormonal fluctuations drive significant variability in systemic immune cell populations
hypotheses.result: Peripheral CD45+, CD4+, CD8+, CD56+, and CD123+ cells remained stable across cycle phases; no hormone-driven fluctuations detected

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cervicovaginal immune responses are sensitive to systemic estradiol levels
hypotheses.result: Cervicovaginal leukocyte abundance positively associated with elevated systemic estradiol during ovulatory phase

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vaginal microbiota composition is sensitive to hormonal cycling
hypotheses.result: Microbial alpha/beta diversity and dominant bacterial genera remained stable; Mobiluncus spp. increased during high-progesterone states; interindividual variability was the primary driver of microbial differences
